correctness.rationale: The fine graph and reduced Markov matrix have equal peripheral data by arxiv:1405.0481 §2. Explicit two-successor calculation produces W=(I+H)P_U/2, where H has k swapped pairs and one fixed point. Closed states are exactly subsets invariant under U and H. If an irreducible W had period d>1, equal-sized cyclic classes each invariant under H would have conflicting parity (one class odd, others even). Thus topological mixing equals transitivity of <U,H>. Classifying permutations by the unique orbit containing the reflection fixed point yields the disjoint integer recurrence. The mirrored coefficients a_{k,j} have an exact ratio (2j+3)/(2k-2j-1), furnishing the uniform middle-tail bounds and verified coefficients 2,3,22. A separately constructed full 2N-state Markov graph agrees for every permutation at N=3,5,7 (5166 exhaustively checked); proof does not rely on finite exhaustion.

value.rationale: The proportion of shuffles preserving topological mixing is a canonical question for precisely the family whose worst mixing and existence of nonmixing are investigated in the motivating literature. The exact all-grid recurrence and sharp three-term rarity law reveal that the nonmixing exceptions occupy 2/N+3/N²+22/N³+O(N^-4) rather than having a positive limiting fraction; this quantitatively resolves a natural gap. The argument isolates a non-obvious automatic-aperiodicity effect of a unique reflection fixed point. This is not a mere change of terminology or special-case restatement of the stretch-and-fold result.
